# 3 Maccabees Chapter 1 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** Ptolemy at Raphia and Jerusalem

---

**1** When Philopator learned from those who returned that the regions he had controlled had been seized by Antiochus, he issued orders to all his forces of infantry and cavalry, took his sister Arsinoe with him, and marched to the regions near Raphia, where Antiochus and his forces were encamped.

**2** But one Theodotus, planning to carry out an act of treachery, took with him the best of the weapons that had been assigned to him, and crossed over by night to Ptolemy's tent, intending to kill him alone and so bring the war to an end.

**3** But Dositheus, known as the son of Drimylus, by birth a Jew, who later changed his religion and turned from the ancestral customs, removed the king and arranged for an unimportant man to sleep in his place in the tent; and it so happened that this was the man Theodotus killed.

**4** When a fierce battle had taken place, and things were looking more favorable for Philopator, Antiochus saw that his situation was serious and that his forces were being overwhelmed.

**5** He withdrew in good order to a position where he could rally his troops.

**6** After the battle Ptolemy reviewed his forces and went to the various cities, exhorting the people and lifting their spirits.

**7** Proceeding in this manner, he came to Judea and to Jerusalem, where he offered sacrifice to the Greatest God as was fitting.

**8** He made thank offerings and performed what was appropriate for the holy place, and then, entering the forecourt, he was struck with admiration at its order and beauty.

**9** He marveled at the arrangement of the temple and resolved that he wished to enter the inner sanctuary.

**10** When they told him that this was not lawful, and that not even any of the priests were permitted to enter, and that not even the high priest entered but once a year, and he alone, Ptolemy was by no means persuaded.

**11** Even after the law had been read out to him he did not cease declaring that he would enter, saying: Even if they are denied this, I should not be denied it.

**12** He asked why, when he had entered all the other temples, no one in those places had prevented him.

**13** Someone answered in an inappropriate manner that his pride in this was wrong.

**14** But since he was about to proceed regardless, the priests together with all the people fell to the ground and begged him to turn aside from this act of impiety.

**15** A great tumult arose throughout the city, and the priests in their vestments threw themselves down before the altar and called out to heaven, imploring assistance in this emergency.

**16** Their cries were heard, and the whole city was filled with weeping and lamentation.

**17** People came rushing out of their houses and crowded together at the most pitiable scene of supplication.

**18** The women had shut themselves in with their children and locked their doors; some leaned out from the windows and others from the rooftops, holding their hands toward heaven and making the most pitiful supplications.

**19** It was a pitiful sight to see the prostration of the whole multitude and the anguish of the high priest in his great distress.

**20** While they were thus calling out and imploring the Almighty Lord to help them in this time of crisis, one of their number, the high priest Shimon, prostrated himself before the sanctuary and prayed in this manner.

**21** O Lord, Lord, King of the heavens and Master of all creation, Holy One among the holy ones, sole Ruler, Almighty, give ear to us who are burdened with suffering caused by a wicked and impure man, puffed up with audacity and strength.

**22** For you, who created all things and govern all, are a righteous Ruler and you judge those who act with violence and arrogance.

**23** You destroyed those in former times who committed unrighteous deeds among whom were also the giants who placed confidence in their strength and boldness, upon whom you brought immeasurable destruction.

**24** You made the Sodomites who acted lawlessly known to all, setting them as an example for those who came afterward.

**25** You made known your great power to the presumptuous Pharaoh who had enslaved your holy people Israel, afflicting them with many and various punishments.

**26** And when he pursued them with chariots and a large army, you drowned him in the depths of the sea, while you brought safely through those who had placed their trust in you, the Ruler of all creation.

**27** And when they had seen your mighty works, they praised you the Almighty.

**28** You, O King, when you created the boundless and immeasurable earth, chose this city and hallowed this place for the glory of your name, though you have need of nothing; and when you had glorified it by your magnificent presence, you established it as the firm foundation for the glory of your great and honored name.

**29** And loving the house of Israel, you promised that if we should fall away and distress should befall us, and we came to this place and prayed, you would hear our prayer.

**30** And you are faithful and true.
